abstract: Maintains vessel positioning certifications, pulling capacity assessments, and towing standby allocation records
system_message:
You are Salvage engineering superintendent (SALV). The salvage engineering superintendent (SALV) maintains vessel positioning certifications, pulling capacity assessments, and towing standby allocation records, as well as emergency mooring gear inspection records for candidate offshore salvage operations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Emergency mooring gear inspection（MOOR）
information_points.content:
SALV-MOOR-AKR：For Semi-submersible vessel tandem tow and wet-docking, emergency mooring gear inspection records document a towing bridle breaking strain of 440 t for the candidate primary towing bridles.
SALV-MOOR-L85：For Emergency buoyancy pontoon stabilization and sheltered escort, emergency mooring gear inspection records show a towing bridle breaking strain of 380 t for the candidate primary towing bridles.
SALV-MOOR-1MU：For Dynamic positioning subsea rigging and heavy-lift retrieval, emergency mooring gear inspection records indicate a towing bridle breaking strain of 320 t for the candidate primary towing bridles.

information_points.title: Maintains vessel positioning certifications, pulling capacity assessments, and towing standby allocation records（TOW）
information_points.content:
SALV-TOW-66D：For Dynamic positioning subsea rigging and heavy-lift retrieval, the primary offshore salvage vessels hold dynamic positioning class 2 certified status, the lead ocean salvage tug has a continuous bollard pull rating of 180 t sustained across a ten-minute static pull trial, and scheduled salvage tug station-keeping standby hours total 50 h.
SALV-TOW-ET9：For Semi-submersible vessel tandem tow and wet-docking, the primary offshore salvage vessels do not hold dynamic positioning class 2 certified status, the lead ocean salvage tug provides a continuous bollard pull rating of 210 t, and scheduled salvage tug station-keeping standby hours amount to 50 h.
SALV-TOW-TCT：For Emergency buoyancy pontoon stabilization and sheltered escort, the primary offshore salvage vessels hold dynamic positioning class 2 certified status, the lead ocean salvage tug achieves a continuous bollard pull rating of 240 t, and scheduled salvage tug station-keeping standby hours total 70 h.
